mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 60% of triggered quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate above 5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market reversal, reducing corporate profit margins and triggering negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for two consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output, which reduces earnings for industrial firms and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 5-year averages signals a dual shock of higher interest rates and inflation, eroding corporate earnings and consumer purchasing power, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: high inflation and high rates regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 0.5% after three consecutive months of decline signals a recovery in consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS monthly change > 0.5% following 3 months of decline
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their 12-month averages signals a labor market expansion with slack absorption, increasing wage pressures and reducing profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -1%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) below 1.2 million units for four consecutive months signals a housing market downturn, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and drags on overall market returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
